transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jia (Redwood CSM), Lina (NovaSearch Head of Search), Mark (NovaSearch CTO), Ravi (Eng Lead), Olivia (PM)

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, uh i'm samir, rubood -- redwood AE, and with me is ethan who will walk through the embeddings + rerank demo.
00:09 Lina: thanks, hi all, lina here. we're evaluating options to improve our search relevance across web and app, current stack is algolia + pinecone for vectors.
00:16 Ethan: great, we'll show the hosted API flow: embeddings for candidate retrieval, then rerank to return the top N by relevance. i'll also show the console where you can see latency / token cost per route.
00:26 Mark: timeline wise, we want a quick POC within 2 weeks, ideally measurable uplift in click-through and time to first result. our main concerns: latency under 150ms p95 and cost per query.
00:38 Ethan: noted. quick architecture: step 1, you send query -> embeddings endpoint to encode the query; step 2, nearest neighbor retrieval in your vector DB (you can keep pinecone or use our vector store) -> step 3, pass top-k candidates into rerank endpoint which scores and returns best doc.
00:55 Ravi: are you doing the nearest neighbor in redwood or do we keep in pinecone?
01:01 Ethan: good q. we let you keep your vector DB, many customers keep pinecone or milvus. the embeddings call is hosted, you get the vector. rerank is a model call that can be run hosted as well - we can also return scores only if you want to do tiebreaking client-side.
01:16 Olivia: what's the typical latency for rerank? we have very high qps on search pages.
01:22 Ethan: for hosted small-to-medium models p95 around 80-140ms depending on sequence length; if you need sub-50ms p95 we usually recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity or lighter rerank model. also batching can help throughput but adds some latency.
01:36 Samir: cost tradeoffs - embeddings per vector vs rerank per token. i'll send a sample pricing sheet. for the POC we can do a capped budget approach.
01:45 Lina: security: we do SOC2 compliant vendors. do you offer KMS & audit logs? we also have data residency requirements for EU.
01:53 Ethan: yes, hosted offers SOC2, audit logs, and KMS integration; for strict residency we can route requests through EU regions, or if needed explore Private (VPC) deployment. we'll share security pack.
02:07 Mark: any red flags around PII in user queries?
02:10 Jia: we recommend token redaction at ingestion, and we persist embeddings only if you choose - default is not to persist. we have customer controls for retention.
02:20 Ethan: demo - switching to screen.
02:23 [screen share]
02:25 Ethan: here is the Console: route management on left, you can see per-route p50/p95 latency, token usage, and cost. this is useful to track search endpoint; you can set per-route policies for fallback to smaller model if high load.
02:40 Ethan: i'll make a sample request to /v1/embeddings. sending query 'best running shoes for trail marathon'
02:46 [terminal]
02:47 Ethan: response in 120ms, vector length 1536, then we do nearest neighbors in pinecone and pass top 8 docs into /v1/rerank model.
03:00 Ravi: are you doing few-shot prompts for rerank?
03:03 Ethan: yes often a small prompt with instructions + doc snippets, we show a couple of prompt templates in the repo i'll share. we also support function/tool calling but for rerank scoring we usually return a numeric score.
03:18 Olivia: what's the format of the rerank response?
03:20 Ethan: we return an ordered list with score and explanation field if you enable structured output. example: [{doc_id:..., score:0.82, highlights: 'contains product model and size info'}] - apologies the transcript might mangle keys, but actual API returns JSON.
03:38 Lina: what's the eval strategy? we need to compare to our current algolia+pinecone baseline.
03:42 Ethan: we recommend a held-out set of queries, run A/B using rerank scoring, measure MRR/CTR. we'll share an eval notebook that runs against your logs and returns metrics.
03:55 Samir: quick note on caching - if you have repeated queries we can do prefix/KV caching to cut costs and latency; optimize will surface suggestions for batching and cache keys.
04:08 Lina: any limits on token length for rerank? some docs are long.
04:12 Ethan: we recommend truncation + smart chunking; rerank only needs salient passages - Optimize can suggest chunk sizes and model variants.
04:21 Mark: ok can we also run a throughput test? say 500 qps for a short window?
04:26 Samir: for hosted we can run bench test but sustained very high qps is better on Dedicated - for POC we can simulate load and measure. we'll coordinate with infra.
04:36 Ethan: walking through sample prompt and cost calc in console. showing cost per rerank call vs embeddings.
04:45 Olivia: curious about cold-starts and model warmup.
04:48 Ethan: KV cache warmup helps; model variants differ. for large rerank models cold p95 can be higher briefly. automatic warmup and reserved capacity on Dedicated helps.
04:58 Lina: acceptance criteria for POC: 5-10% increase in CTR or MRR improvement over baseline, p95 < 150ms, cost under provided budget.
05:07 Samir: perfect, we'll propose scope: 2 week pilot, ingest 1k queries, run eval notebook, return metrics, then discuss Dedicated if results good.
05:15 Mark: who owns SLA during pilot?
05:18 Jia: for pilot it's best-effort but we'll provide escalation and dedicated SE hours.
05:23 Samir: ok let's recap action items.
05:27 Samir: lina, you'll send sample logs; ethan will send eval notebook; i'll send pricing and security docs; propose kickoff for 11/30.
05:36 Lina: sounds good, thanks everyone.
05:38 Samir: thanks all.
[call ends]
